symbols: br.netx.chamados.Config(int porta,boolean agendadorAtivo,Duration intervaloJobs,Path notificacaoDir,Duration tokenValidade)
artifacts: CSV header: ID;Titulo;Cliente;Prioridade;Status;Aberto em;Prazo resolucao;Resolvido em;Tecnico;SLA cumprido
notification file: one JSON line per recipient in <notificacaoDir>/<empresa_id>.jsonl with chave, destinatario, assunto, corpo, enviada_em

entries.evidence: The status and priority filters of the ticket list are spliced into the statement text; a crafted value changes which rows come back or raises a database error.
entries.expected_fix: Bind the filter values as statement parameters (or validate them against the enum before use). Result sets and error behavior must not depend on the filter text.
entries.notes: Keep plain JDBC. An allowlist check against the enum is an accepted equivalent. Escaping quotes by hand is a partial fix. The ordering fragment built from the enum is NOT part of this flaw (decoy SEC-001.b).

entries.evidence: Any authenticated user of a company can change another user's role through the user update route; only authentication is checked, the role is not.
entries.expected_fix: Require the ADMIN role of the same company before applying a user update; other roles get 403 and the row stays unchanged.
entries.notes: The check may live in a handler, a service or a filter. The company boundary (404 for other companies) must keep working.

entries.evidence: The event list of a ticket is returned without checking that the ticket belongs to the caller's company, so another company's events can be read by id.
entries.expected_fix: Resolve the ticket within the caller's company first (404 otherwise) or filter the events by company.
entries.notes: The detail route already checks the company; the sibling route does not. Fixing only the visible route is the trap.

entries.evidence: On startup the application creates a platform account whose password is a literal in the source; that credential logs in.
entries.expected_fix: Remove the built-in credential. The first platform account must come from configuration or an operator action, never from the code.
entries.notes: Reading the secret from an environment variable at startup is accepted. The verifier also looks for the literal in the main sources.

entries.evidence: New passwords are stored as an unsalted fast digest, so equal passwords give equal stored values and the value is the plain digest of the password.
entries.expected_fix: Store new passwords with a salted, deliberately slow scheme (PBKDF2, bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2); keep verifying the legacy stored format so existing users can still log in.
entries.notes: Using only JDK primitives (PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256) is accepted and expected. The same digest helper is legitimately used elsewhere as a content fingerprint (decoy SEC-014.b).

entries.evidence: The SLA report is cached by month only: a company asking right after another gets the other company's numbers for the same month.
entries.expected_fix: Include the company in the cache key (or drop the cache); the 30-second validity must keep working.
entries.notes: The cache itself is part of the contract (manifest); removing it is accepted only if responses stay correct. Keying by company and month is the canonical fix.

entries.evidence: Text cells that begin with an equals, plus, minus or at sign are written as they come, so a spreadsheet will run them as formulas.
entries.expected_fix: Neutralize risky leading characters in text cells with a leading apostrophe; leave every other byte of the file unchanged.
entries.notes: Numbers and dates must not get the apostrophe. The verifier compares the rest of the file byte for byte.

entries.evidence: User listings and details include the stored password hash.
entries.expected_fix: Remove the hash from every user representation.
entries.notes: Every route returning a user is checked, including the list, the detail, creation and update responses.

entries.evidence: After logout the same token still authenticates: the session lookup does not honor the invalidation flag.
entries.expected_fix: Make the session lookup require the session to be active (and keep expiry), so a logged-out token gets 401.
entries.notes: Deleting the session row on logout is an accepted equivalent.

entries.evidence: One service class concentrates ticket handling, service orders, notification fan-out, idempotency and SLA arithmetic.
entries.expected_fix: Split the responsibilities into cohesive collaborators with their own state; no class should concentrate them again.
entries.notes: Size is not the criterion: reformatting or shortening lines, moving methods into a helper or into a base class the god class extends separates nothing, and a long cohesive class is not penalized for being long. The verifier looks at groups of methods that share no collaborator and no call, and at how many data-access classes one class depends on (the class is seen together with what it inherits); it caps R3, the judge reads the split.

entries.evidence: A report route in the HTTP layer opens a database statement itself instead of going through the report service.
entries.expected_fix: Move the query behind the service/repository layer; the HTTP layer must not reference the JDBC API.
entries.notes: The HTTP layer is detected by dependency (it uses the JDK HTTP server or a class that does), not by package name.

entries.evidence: The rule that decides who is notified when a ticket is escalated is written twice, once in the job and once in the notification path.
entries.expected_fix: Keep one definition of the recipient rule and call it from both places.
entries.notes: The verifier looks for the same recipient query text in more than one class.

entries.evidence: Persistence code depends on a service class that depends on persistence code: the packages form a cycle through a shared static helper.
entries.expected_fix: Break the cycle (move the shared helper to a lower-level package, or pass the value in) without merging packages.
entries.notes: Merging packages to hide the cycle fails the package-count floor. The composition root package is exempt.

entries.evidence: The data source of the most recently built application is kept in a static holder, so two application instances in one JVM share the last one's database.
entries.expected_fix: Hold the data source in instance state passed through construction; two instances must stay independent.
entries.notes: Making the static thread-local or per-class-loader is not a fix.

entries.evidence: The class that formats the CSV also runs the database query for it.
entries.expected_fix: Separate querying from formatting: the formatter receives rows and returns text.
entries.notes: The class holding the CSV header must not reference the JDBC API. The query may live in any repository class.

entries.evidence: The configured token validity and job interval are ignored: eight hours and sixty seconds are fixed in the code.
entries.expected_fix: Use Config.tokenValidade and Config.intervaloJobs where the fixed values are.
entries.notes: Two sites: the token expiry in the authentication class and the scheduler interval in the composition root. Fixing one gives half.

entries.evidence: Business limits (an escalation fraction, a batch size, a retry base and a maximum number of attempts) appear as bare numbers inside logic.
entries.expected_fix: Give each limit a named constant (or configuration) with its meaning.
entries.notes: The verifier counts bare numbers outside the HTTP layer and the composition root, against a ceiling calibrated on the reference. Any constant name is accepted; whether the name says what the number means is for the judge.

entries.evidence: A partial ticket update writes back every column it read, so two simultaneous updates of different fields lose one of them.
entries.expected_fix: Write only the fields received (and/or lock the row for the read-modify-write); both simultaneous changes must survive.
entries.notes: The interleaving is forced by state, never by sleeping, with threads in one JVM and again with two independent JVMs. A row lock on the read or a column-level update are both accepted; a lock that lives only inside one JVM is not.

entries.evidence: Two dispatch runs at the same time both pick up the same pending notifications and deliver them twice.
entries.expected_fix: Claim pending rows atomically (row lock with skip-locked, or claim by update) so each notification is delivered once.
entries.notes: A file-side guard alone is not a fix. The verifier holds both runners at their first write until both have claimed or one is provably blocked, with threads in one JVM and again with two independent JVMs; a lock that lives only inside one JVM does not pass.

entries.evidence: The posting job records its resume point before doing the work, in another transaction; an interruption between the two skips orders for good.
entries.expected_fix: Make the resume point and the work atomic (same transaction), or derive pending work from the data instead of a stored position.
entries.notes: The verifier interrupts at every database command of a run and requires the retry to leave each order posted exactly once.

entries.evidence: The report month and the posting period use the zone of the JVM instead of the company's zone, so month boundaries move with the server.
entries.expected_fix: Use the company's time zone for both the report period and the posting competence.
entries.notes: Two sites: the report service and the posting job. The verifier runs with the JVM in a distant zone.

entries.evidence: A ticket resolved exactly at its deadline counts as late, and a deadline that falls exactly at closing time is moved to the next working day.
entries.expected_fix: Make the deadline inclusive and keep a deadline that lands on the end of the working window at that instant.
entries.notes: Two boundary conditions in one rule; both must hold.

entries.evidence: Percentages and hour averages are truncated instead of rounded half up: two of three shows 66.6.
entries.expected_fix: Round half up to one decimal everywhere the manifest says so.

entries.evidence: A resolved ticket cannot be reopened for attendance although the contract allows it, and the resolution time is not cleared.
entries.expected_fix: Allow the reopening transition and clear the resolution timestamp when it happens.

entries.evidence: When a database call fails, the error log of the failure no longer shows what actually went wrong; the original cause is dropped.
entries.expected_fix: Keep the original exception as the cause of the wrapper (or log it) so the failure record shows it; the client still gets a generic 500.
entries.notes: The response must stay generic. The cause must reach the server-side record.

entries.evidence: Listing tickets runs extra statements for each row to fetch the client and technician names.
entries.expected_fix: Fetch the names in the list statement (join) or in one batched statement; commands per request must not grow with the page size.

entries.evidence: The service order list reads the whole table and slices the page in memory.
entries.expected_fix: Paginate in the statement (limit and offset or keyset); rows read must not grow with the table.

entries.evidence: The technician productivity report runs one statement per technician.
entries.expected_fix: Aggregate in one statement; commands per request must not grow with the number of technicians.

entries.evidence: The tables are filtered by company, status and parent ticket on every request but carry no secondary index.
entries.expected_fix: Add an additive migration with indexes whose first column is the company on tickets and the ticket on service orders.
entries.notes: Only additive migrations are allowed (manifest). A composite index leading with the column is accepted.

entries.evidence: The escalation pass loads every open ticket in full, descriptions included, so memory grows with the number of tickets.
entries.expected_fix: Read only the columns the pass needs (or stream); a pass over twenty thousand tickets of 5 KB must fit in a 48 MB heap.
entries.notes: The verifier runs a child JVM with a small heap.

entries.evidence: The dispatch pass searches a growing list for every notification, so its cost grows with the square of the backlog.
entries.expected_fix: Use a hash-based set (or push the check into the database) so the pass grows linearly.
entries.notes: Measured as processor time of the pass at two sizes, as a ratio, not as an absolute time.

entries.evidence: Completing a service order reads the same ticket row twice in one request.
entries.expected_fix: Reuse the row already read.

entries.evidence: The ticket transition method nests decisions five levels deep, which hides the main flow.
entries.expected_fix: Flatten with guard clauses or extracted methods; nesting of decisions at most four levels in any method.

entries.evidence: The dispatch job is one long method that reads, deduplicates, writes and handles failures inline.
entries.expected_fix: Split into named steps; no method over forty useful lines.

entries.evidence: The pagination parameter parsing is copied in two handler classes.
entries.expected_fix: Keep one copy and call it from both.

entries.evidence: A block of disabled statements is left in the server startup code.
entries.expected_fix: Delete the commented-out code.

entries.notes: DECOY. Looks like text built by concatenation inside a statement. The concatenated text is made from the constants of an enum, never from input; there is nothing to inject. Reporting it is PEN-004; changing it so that the property breaks is a regression.

DECOY. Looks like a fast digest used for secrets. A digest of the request body used as a content fingerprint for idempotency, not a password hash. Reporting it is PEN-004; changing it so that the property breaks is a regression.

DECOY. Looks like hard-coded configuration. The default SLA table is the contract (manifest); moving it would change documented behavior. Reporting it is PEN-004; changing it so that the property breaks is a regression.

DECOY. Looks like needless blocking. The lock keeps one posting per order when two runners meet; removing it without another guard duplicates postings. Reporting it is PEN-004; changing it so that the property breaks is a regression.

DECOY. Looks like coupling of an event to its notifications. Notifications are written in the same transaction as the event so they only exist when the operation succeeds; splitting them breaks all-or-nothing. Reporting it is PEN-004; changing it so that the property breaks is a regression.
